latin: Avia Pieridum peragro loca nullius ante
en: I range through the pathless places of the Pierides, trodden before

latin: trita solo. iuvat integros accedere fontis
en: by no one's foot. It is a joy to come to untouched springs

latin: atque haurire, iuvatque novos decerpere flores
en: and drink from them, a joy to pluck new flowers

latin: insignemque meo capiti petere inde coronam,
en: and to seek for my head a crown of distinction from there

latin: unde prius nulli velarint tempora musae;
en: where the Muses have veiled no one's temples before;

latin: primum quod magnis doceo de rebus et artis
en: first because I teach of great things, and go on

latin: religionum animum nodis exsolvere pergo,
en: to free the mind from the tight-tied knots of religion,

latin: deinde quod obscura de re tam lucida pango
en: then because on a dark matter I compose such lucid

latin: carmina musaeo contingens cuncta lepore.
en: verses, touching all of it with the Muses' charm.

latin: id quoque enim non ab nulla ratione videtur;
en: For this too seems not to be without good reason;

latin: nam vel uti pueris absinthia taetra medentes
en: for just as physicians, with foul wormwood for children,

latin: cum dare conantur, prius oras pocula circum
en: when they try to give it, first touch the rims round the cups

latin: contingunt mellis dulci flavoque liquore,
en: with the sweet and golden liquid of honey,

latin: ut puerorum aetas inprovida ludificetur
en: so that the unforeseeing age of children may be fooled

latin: labrorum tenus, interea perpotet amarum
en: as far as the lips, and meanwhile drink down the bitter

latin: absinthi laticem deceptaque non capiatur,
en: juice of wormwood, and, deceived, may not be undone,

latin: sed potius tali facto recreata valescat,
en: but rather, restored by such means, may grow strong,

latin: sic ego nunc, quoniam haec ratio plerumque videtur
en: so I now, since this reasoning often seems

latin: tristior esse quibus non est tractata, retroque
en: rather grim to those who have not handled it, and the crowd

latin: volgus abhorret ab hac, volui tibi suaviloquenti
en: shrinks back from it, have wished, in sweet-speaking

latin: carmine Pierio rationem exponere nostram
en: Pierian song, to set out for you our reasoning

latin: et quasi musaeo dulci contingere melle;
en: and, as it were, to touch it with the Muses' sweet honey,

latin: si tibi forte animum tali ratione tenere
en: if by such means I might perhaps hold your mind

latin: versibus in nostris possem, dum percipis omnem
en: on our verses, while you perceive the whole

latin: naturam rerum ac persentis utilitatem.
en: nature of things and feel its usefulness through and through.

latin: Sed quoniam docui cunctarum exordia rerum
en: But since I have taught what the origins of all things

latin: qualia sint et quam variis distantia formis
en: are like, and how, differing in their various shapes,

latin: sponte sua volitent aeterno percita motu
en: they fly of their own accord, driven by eternal motion,

latin: quoque modo possit res ex his quaeque creari,
en: and in what way each thing can be created from them,

latin: nunc agere incipiam tibi quod vehementer ad has res
en: I shall now begin to treat for you what bears closely on these things:

latin: attinet esse ea quae rerum simulacra vocamus,
en: that there exist what we call the images of things,

latin: quae quasi membranae vel cortex nominitandast,
en: which are to be named, as it were, films or bark;

latin: atque animi quoniam docui natura quid esset
en: and since I have taught what the nature of the mind is,

latin: et quibus e rebus cum corpore compta vigeret
en: and from what things, joined with the body, it is made and thrives,

latin: quove modo distracta rediret in ordia prima,
en: and in what way, torn apart, it returns to its first-beginnings,

latin: nunc agere incipiam tibi, quod vehementer ad has res
en: I shall now begin to treat for you what bears closely on these things:

latin: attinet esse ea quae rerum simulacra vocamus,
en: that there exist what we call the images of things,

latin: quod speciem ac formam similem gerit eius imago,
en: because the image carries a likeness and form like that thing's

latin: cuius cumque cluet de corpore fusa vagari;
en: from whose body, whatever it is, it is said to be shed and wander;

latin: quae quasi membranae summo de corpore rerum
en: which, like films torn from the outermost body of things,

latin: dereptae volitant ultroque citroque per auras,
en: fly this way and that through the air,

latin: atque eadem nobis vigilantibus obvia mentes
en: and these same, meeting us when we are awake, terrify

latin: terrificant atque in somnis, cum saepe figuras
en: our minds, and in sleep too, when often we behold shapes

latin: contuimur miras simulacraque luce carentum,
en: strange to see, and the images of those who lack the light,

latin: quae nos horrifice languentis saepe sopore
en: which have often roused us in horror as we lay languid

latin: excierunt ne forte animas Acherunte reamur
en: in sleep: lest we should think by chance that spirits escape

latin: effugere aut umbras inter vivos volitare
en: from Acheron, or that shades fly among the living,

latin: neve aliquid nostri post mortem posse relinqui,
en: or that something of us can be left behind after death,

latin: cum corpus simul atque animi natura perempta
en: when the body and the nature of the mind, destroyed together,

latin: in sua discessum dederint primordia quaeque.
en: have gone their separate ways, each into its own first-beginnings.

latin: dico igitur rerum effigias tenuisque figuras
en: I say, therefore, that effigies of things and thin shapes

latin: mittier ab rebus summo de cortice eorum;
en: are sent off from things, from their outermost bark;

latin: id licet hinc quamvis hebeti cognoscere corde.
en: which one may come to know from this, however dull one's heart.

latin: Principio quoniam mittunt in rebus apertis
en: To begin with, since among things open to view many things

latin: corpora res multae, partim diffusa solute,
en: send off bodies, some diffused loosely abroad,

latin: robora ceu fumum mittunt ignesque vaporem,
en: as logs send off smoke and fires heat,

latin: et partim contexta magis condensaque, ut olim
en: and some more closely woven and dense, as when at times

latin: cum teretis ponunt tunicas aestate cicadae,
en: cicadas put off their smooth coats in summer,

latin: et vituli cum membranas de corpore summo
en: and when calves at birth send off films

latin: nascentes mittunt, et item cum lubrica serpens
en: from the outermost body, and again when the slippery serpent

latin: exuit in spinis vestem; nam saepe videmus
en: strips off its garment among the thorns; for we often see

latin: illorum spoliis vepres volitantibus auctas.
en: the brambles decked with their fluttering spoils.

latin: quae quoniam fiunt, tenuis quoque debet imago
en: And since these things happen, a thin image too must

latin: ab rebus mitti summo de corpore rerum.
en: be sent off from things, from the outermost body of things.

latin: nam cur illa cadant magis ab rebusque recedant
en: For why those should fall and withdraw from things more

latin: quam quae tenvia sunt, hiscendist nulla potestas;
en: than those that are thin, there is no power to open one's mouth;

latin: praesertim cum sint in summis corpora rebus
en: especially since on the surface of things there are bodies

latin: multa minuta, iaci quae possint ordine eodem
en: many and minute, which could be thrown off in the same order

latin: quo fuerint et formai servare figuram,
en: they had before and keep the outline of the form,

latin: et multo citius, quanto minus indupediri
en: and much more swiftly, inasmuch as they can be less hindered,

latin: pauca queunt et quae sunt prima fronte locata.
en: being few and placed in the very front.

latin: nam certe iacere ac largiri multa videmus,
en: For certainly we see many things throw off and give out,

latin: non solum ex alto penitusque, ut diximus ante,
en: not only from the depth and from within, as we said before,

latin: verum de summis ipsum quoque saepe colorem.
en: but from the surface, often, the very color too.

latin: et volgo faciunt id lutea russaque vela
en: And this is commonly done by awnings, yellow and red

latin: et ferrugina, cum magnis intenta theatris
en: and dark blue, when stretched over great theaters

latin: per malos volgata trabesque trementia flutant;
en: they flap and quiver, spread out on masts and beams;

latin: namque ibi consessum caveai supter et omnem
en: for there the assembly seated in the tiers beneath, and all

latin: scaenai speciem patrum matrumque deorsum
en: the face of the stage, the fathers and the mothers down below,

latin: inficiunt coguntque suo fluitare colore.
en: they stain, and make them ripple with their color.

latin: et quanto circum mage sunt inclusa theatri
en: And the more closely the walls of the theater are shut in

latin: moenia, tam magis haec intus perfusa lepore
en: all around, the more everything inside, steeped in charm,

latin: omnia conrident correpta luce diei.
en: laughs, now that the light of day is pent within.

latin: ergo lintea de summo cum corpore fucum
en: Therefore, since linens send off a dye from their surface,

latin: mittunt, effigias quoque debent mittere tenvis
en: each thing too must send off thin effigies,

latin: res quaeque, ex summo quoniam iaculantur utraque.
en: since in both cases they are thrown from the surface.

latin: sunt igitur iam formarum vestigia certa,
en: There are therefore by now sure traces of forms,

latin: quae volgo volitant subtili praedita filo
en: which commonly fly about, endowed with a fine thread,

latin: nec singillatim possunt secreta videri.
en: and cannot be seen one by one, apart.

latin: Praeterea omnis odor fumus vapor atque aliae res
en: Further, every smell, smoke, heat, and other things

latin: consimiles ideo diffusae rebus abundant,
en: of the kind stream out from things diffused for this reason:

latin: ex alto quia dum veniunt extrinsecus ortae
en: because while they come out from the depths, risen to the outside,

latin: scinduntur per iter flexum, nec recta viarum
en: they are torn apart on their winding path, and there are no straight

latin: ostia sunt, qua contendant exire coortae.
en: mouths to the roads by which, once risen, they can strive to get out.

latin: at contra tenuis summi membrana coloris
en: But on the other hand, when a thin film of surface color

latin: cum iacitur, nihil est quod eam discerpere possit,
en: is thrown off, there is nothing that can tear it apart,

latin: in promptu quoniam est in prima fronte locata.
en: since it is ready at hand, placed in the very front.

latin: Postremo speculis in aqua splendoreque in omni
en: Finally, whatever images appear to us in mirrors,

latin: quae cumque apparent nobis simulacra, necessest,
en: in water, and in every shining surface, must,

latin: quandoquidem simili specie sunt praedita rerum,
en: since they are endowed with a likeness like that of things,

latin: exin imaginibus missis consistere eorum.
en: consist of images sent off from those things.

latin: nam cur illa cadant magis ab rebusque recedant
en: For why those should fall and withdraw from things more

latin: quam quae tenuia sunt, hiscendist nulla potestas.
en: than those that are thin, there is no power to open one's mouth.

latin: sunt igitur tenues formarum illis similesque
en: There are therefore thin effigies of forms, and like them,

latin: effigiae, singillatim quas cernere nemo
en: which, though no one can make them out

latin: cum possit, tamen adsiduo crebroque repulsu
en: one by one, yet thrown back by constant and repeated rebounding

latin: reiectae reddunt speculorum ex aequore visum,
en: return a sight from the level surface of mirrors;

latin: nec ratione alia servari posse videntur,
en: and in no other way, it seems, could they be preserved

latin: tanto opere ut similes reddantur cuique figurae.
en: so that shapes so like each thing are returned.

latin: Nunc age, quam tenui natura constet imago
en: Come now, how thin a nature the image is made of,

latin: percipe. et in primis, quoniam primordia tantum
en: learn. And in the first place, since the first-beginnings are so far

latin: sunt infra nostros sensus tantoque minora
en: beneath our senses, and so much smaller

latin: quam quae primum oculi coeptant non posse tueri,
en: than those things which the eyes first begin to be unable to see,

latin: nunc tamen id quoque uti confirmem, exordia rerum
en: yet now, so that I may confirm this too, how fine the origins

latin: cunctarum quam sint subtilia percipe paucis.
en: of all things are, learn in a few words.

latin: primum animalia sunt iam partim tantula, corum
en: First, there are living creatures already so tiny that a third part

latin: tertia pars nulla possit ratione videri.
en: of them could by no means be seen.

latin: horum intestinum quodvis quale esse putandumst!
en: What must one think any one of their entrails is like!

latin: quid cordis globus aut oculi? quid membra? quid artus?
en: What of the heart's ball, or the eye's? What of the limbs? The joints?

latin: quantula sunt! quid praeterea primordia quaeque,
en: How tiny they are! And what, further, of each first-beginning

latin: unde anima atque animi constet natura necessumst,
en: of which the spirit and the nature of the mind must consist?

latin: nonne vides quam sint subtilia quamque minuta?
en: Do you not see how fine they are, and how minute?

latin: praeterea quaecumque suo de corpore odorem
en: Further, whatever things breathe out from their bodies

latin: expirant acrem, panaces absinthia taetra
en: a sharp smell, the panacea, foul wormwood,

latin: habrotonique graves et tristia centaurea,
en: strong-smelling southernwood, and grim centaury,

latin: quorum unum quidvis leviter si forte duobus
en: of which any one, if by chance lightly between two

latin: quin potius noscas rerum simulacra vagari
en: Why not rather recognize that images of things wander about,

latin: multa modis multis, nulla vi cassaque sensu?
en: many, in many ways, with no force, and void of sense?

latin: Sed ne forte putes ea demum sola vagari,
en: But lest you perhaps think that only those wander about,

latin: quae cumque ab rebus rerum simulacra recedunt,
en: whatever images of things withdraw from things,

latin: sunt etiam quae sponte sua gignuntur et ipsa
en: there are also those that are born of their own accord and themselves

latin: constituuntur in hoc caelo, qui dicitur aer,
en: take shape in this sky, which is called air,

latin: quae multis formata modis sublime feruntur,
en: which, formed in many ways, are borne on high,

latin: ut nubes facile inter dum concrescere in alto
en: as we see clouds at times easily gather on high

latin: cernimus et mundi speciem violare serenam
en: and mar the calm face of the world,

latin: aeraaëra mulcentes motu; nam saepe Gigantum
en: caressing the air with their motion; for often the faces of Giants

latin: ora volare videntur et umbram ducere late,
en: seem to fly and draw a shadow far and wide,

latin: inter dum magni montes avolsaque saxa
en: at times great mountains and rocks torn from

latin: montibus ante ire et solem succedere praeter,
en: the mountains seem to go before and pass across the sun,

latin: inde alios trahere atque inducere belua nimbos.
en: then a beast to drag and draw on other storm-clouds.

latin: nec speciem mutare suam liquentia cessant
en: Nor do they cease, melting, to change their likeness

latin: et cuiusque modi formarum vertere in oras.
en: and turn into the outlines of forms of every kind.

latin: Nunc ea quam facili et celeri ratione genantur
en: Now, by how easy and how swift a principle these are produced,

latin: perpetuoque fluant ab rebus lapsaque cedant
en: and how they flow perpetually from things and slip off and withdraw,

latin: semper enim summum quicquid de rebus abundat,
en: for always there is something streaming off the surface of things

latin: quod iaculentur. et hoc alias cum pervenit in res,
en: for them to cast away. And when this reaches other things,

latin: transit, ut in primis vestem; sed ubi aspera saxa
en: it passes through, as above all through cloth; but when it meets rough rocks

latin: aut in materiam ligni pervenit, ibi iam
en: or comes upon the matter of wood, there at once

latin: scinditur, ut nullum simulacrum reddere possit.
en: it is torn apart, so that it can give back no image.

latin: at cum splendida quae constant opposta fuerunt
en: But when things that are bright and dense are set against it,

latin: densaque, ut in primis speculum est, nihil accidit horum;
en: as above all a mirror is, none of this befalls;

latin: nam neque, uti vestem, possunt transire, neque autem
en: for it can neither pass through them, as through cloth, nor yet

latin: scindi; quam meminit levor praestare salutem.
en: be torn apart; a safety their smoothness never fails to secure.

latin: qua propter fit ut hinc nobis simulacra redundent.
en: And that is why the images stream back to us from there.

latin: et quamvis subito quovis in tempore quamque
en: And however suddenly, at whatever time, you set

latin: rem contra speculum ponas, apparet imago;
en: any thing against a mirror, an image appears;

latin: perpetuo fluere ut noscas e corpore summo
en: so you may know that from the surface there flow perpetually

latin: texturas rerum tenuis tenuisque figuras.
en: thin textures of things and thin shapes.

latin: ergo multa brevi spatio simulacra genuntur,
en: Therefore many images are produced in a brief space,

latin: ut merito celer his rebus dicatur origo.
en: so that the origin of these things may rightly be called swift.

latin: et quasi multa brevi spatio summittere debet
en: And just as the sun must send up many lights

latin: lumina sol, ut perpetuo sint omnia plena,
en: in a brief space, so that all things may be perpetually full,

latin: sic ab rebus item simili ratione necessest
en: so likewise, on a like principle, it must be that from things

latin: temporis in puncto rerum simulacra ferantur
en: in a moment of time images of things are carried,

latin: multa modis multis in cunctas undique partis;
en: many, in many ways, in all directions on every side;

latin: quandoquidem speculum quo cumque obvertimus oris,
en: since to whatever quarter we turn a mirror's face,

latin: res ibi respondent simili forma atque colore.
en: things answer there with like shape and like color.

latin: Praeterea modo cum fuerit liquidissima caeli
en: Further, when the weather of the sky has just been at its clearest,

latin: tempestas, perquam subito fit turbida foede,
en: quite suddenly it turns foully turbid,

latin: undique uti tenebras omnis Acherunta rearis
en: so that you would think all the darkness on every side had left

latin: liquisse et magnas caeli complesse cavernas.
en: Acheron and filled the great caverns of the sky.

latin: usque adeo taetra nimborum nocte coorta
en: So utterly, when the hideous night of storm clouds has risen,

latin: inpendent atrae Formidinis ora superne;
en: do the faces of black Terror hang over us from above;

latin: quorum quantula pars sit imago dicere nemost
en: yet how tiny a part of these an image is, there is no one

latin: qui possit neque eam rationem reddere dictis.
en: who could say, or render an account of it in words.

latin: Nunc age, quam celeri motu simulacra ferantur,
en: Come now, with what swift motion the images are carried,

latin: et quae mobilitas ollis tranantibus auras
en: and what mobility is granted them as they swim through the air,

latin: reddita sit, longo spatio ut brevis hora teratur,
en: so that a long distance is worn away in a brief hour,

latin: in quem quaeque locum diverso numine tendunt,
en: toward whatever place each strains with its diverse bent,

latin: suavidicis potius quam multis versibus edam;
en: I shall set out in verses sweet-spoken rather than many;

latin: parvus ut est cycni melior canor, ille gruum quam
en: as the small song of the swan is better than that clamor

latin: clamor in aetheriis dispersus nubibus austri.
en: of cranes scattered among the high clouds of the south wind.

latin: Principio persaepe levis res atque minutis
en: To begin with, very often one may see that things that are light

latin: corporibus factas celeris licet esse videre.
en: and made of minute bodies are swift.

latin: in quo iam genere est solis lux et vapor eius,
en: Of this kind is the light of the sun and its heat,

latin: propterea quia sunt e primis facta minutis,
en: because they are made of minute first bodies

latin: quae quasi cuduntur perque aerisaëris intervallum
en: which are, as it were, hammered on, and through the interval of air

latin: non dubitant transire sequenti concita plaga;
en: do not hesitate to pass, driven on by the blow that follows;

latin: suppeditatur enim confestim lumine lumen
en: for at once light is supplied by light,

latin: et quasi protelo stimulatur fulgere fulgur.
en: and flash is goaded on by flash, as if by a team in tandem.

latin: qua propter simulacra pari ratione necessest
en: Therefore images, on a like principle, must

latin: inmemorabile per spatium transcurrere posse
en: be able to run across a space beyond telling

latin: temporis in puncto, primum quod parvola causa
en: in a moment of time, first because there is a very small cause

latin: est procul a tergo quae provehat atque propellat,
en: far behind them to carry them forward and drive them on,

latin: quod super est, ubi tam volucri levitate ferantur,
en: for the rest, since they are carried with so winged a lightness;

latin: deinde quod usque adeo textura praedita rara
en: next, because they are sent out endowed with so rare

latin: mittuntur, facile ut quasvis penetrare queant res
en: a texture that they can easily penetrate any things

latin: et quasi permanare per aerisaëris intervallum.
en: and, as it were, seep through the interval of air.

latin: Praeterea si quae penitus corpuscula rerum
en: Further, if those small bodies of things that from deep within

latin: ex altoque foras mittuntur, solis uti lux
en: and from far inside are sent out, like the sun's light

latin: ac vapor, haec puncto cernuntur lapsa diei
en: and heat, are seen in a moment of the day to glide

latin: per totum caeli spatium diffundere sese
en: and spread themselves through the whole space of heaven

latin: perque volare mare ac terras caelumque rigare.
en: and fly across sea and lands and flood the sky,

latin: quid quae sunt igitur iam prima fronte parata,
en: what then of those that stand ready at the very front,

latin: cum iaciuntur et emissum res nulla moratur?
en: when they are cast off and nothing hinders their release?

latin: quone vides citius debere et longius ire
en: Do you not see how much more swiftly and farther they must go

latin: multiplexque loci spatium transcurrere eodem
en: and run through many times the extent of space in the same

latin: tempore quo solis pervolgant lumina caelum?
en: time in which the sun's lights spread through heaven.

latin: Hoc etiam in primis specimen verum esse videtur,
en: This too above all seems a true proof

latin: quam celeri motu rerum simulacra ferantur,
en: of how swift the motion is with which images of things are carried:

latin: quod simul ac primum sub diu splendor aquai
en: that as soon as a gleaming sheet of water is laid down

latin: ponitur, extemplo caelo stellante serena
en: under the open sky, at once, when the sky is starry, the calm

latin: sidera respondent in aqua radiantia mundi.
en: stars of the world answer, radiant in the water.

latin: iamne vides igitur quam puncto tempore imago
en: Now do you see, then, in what a moment of time an image

latin: aetheris ex oris in terrarum accidat oras?
en: falls from the shores of the ether to the shores of the earth?

latin: quare etiam atque etiam mitti fateare necessest
en: Therefore again and again you must confess that bodies

latin: corpora quae feriant oculos visumque lacessant.
en: are sent out that strike the eyes and provoke the sight.

latin: perpetuoque fluunt certis ab rebus odores,
en: And from certain things odors flow perpetually,

latin: frigus ut a fluviis, calor ab sole, aestus ab undis
en: as cold from rivers, heat from the sun, from the waves of the sea

latin: aequoris, exesor moerorum litora circum,
en: the surge, the eater of walls along the shores,

latin: nec variae cessant voces volitare per auras.
en: and various voices never cease to fly through the air.

latin: denique in os salsi venit umor saepe saporis,
en: Finally, a moisture of salty flavor often comes into the mouth

latin: cum mare versamur propter, dilutaque contra
en: when we walk beside the sea, and when we watch

latin: cum tuimur misceri absinthia, tangit amaror.
en: wormwood being diluted and mixed, its bitterness touches us.

latin: usque adeo omnibus ab rebus res quaeque fluenter
en: So true is it that from all things each thing is carried off

latin: fertur et in cunctas dimittitur undique partis
en: in a stream, and sent away in all directions on every side,

latin: nec mora nec requies interdatur ulla fluendi,
en: and no delay, no rest is granted in the flowing,

latin: perpetuo quoniam sentimus et omnia semper
en: since we perpetually feel, and may always

latin: cernere odorari licet et sentire sonare.
en: see all things, smell them, and sense them sounding.

latin: Praeterea quoniam manibus tractata figura
en: Further, since a certain shape, handled with the hands

latin: in tenebris quaedam cognoscitur esse eadem quae
en: in the dark, is known to be the same as the one

latin: cernitur in luce et claro candore, necessest
en: seen in the light and the clear brightness, it must be

latin: consimili causa tactum visumque moveri.
en: that touch and sight are moved by a like cause.

latin: nunc igitur si quadratum temptamus et id nos
en: Now then, if we feel a square thing and it

latin: commovet in tenebris, in luci quae poterit res
en: stirs us in the dark, what thing in the light could

latin: accidere ad speciem quadrata, nisi eius imago?
en: fall square upon our sight, if not its image?

latin: esse in imaginibus qua propter causa videtur
en: Therefore the cause of seeing is seen to lie

latin: cernundi neque posse sine his res ulla videri.
en: in images, and without them no thing can be seen.

latin: Nunc ea quae dico rerum simulacra feruntur
en: Now these which I call images of things are carried

latin: undique et in cunctas iaciuntur didita partis;
en: everywhere, and are cast out spread in all directions;

latin: verum nos oculis quia solis cernere quimus,
en: but because we can see with the eyes alone,

latin: propterea fit uti, speciem quo vertimus, omnes
en: it comes about that wherever we turn our gaze, all things

latin: res ibi eam contra feriant forma atque colore.
en: there strike against it with shape and color.

latin: et quantum quaeque ab nobis res absit, imago
en: And how far each thing stands away from us, the image

latin: efficit ut videamus et internoscere curat;
en: makes us see, and takes care that we distinguish it;

latin: nam cum mittitur, extemplo protrudit agitque
en: for when it is sent off, at once it thrusts and drives before it

latin: aeraaëra qui inter se cumque est oculosque locatus,
en: whatever air is placed between itself and the eyes,

latin: isque ita per nostras acies perlabitur omnis
en: and so all this air glides through our eyes

latin: et quasi perterget pupillas atque ita transit.
en: and, as it were, sweeps the pupils, and so passes through.

latin: propterea fit uti videamus quam procul absit
en: That is why we see how far off each thing

latin: res quaeque. et quanto plus aerisaëris ante agitatur
en: stands. And the more air is driven on before it,

latin: et nostros oculos perterget longior aura,
en: and the longer the breeze that sweeps our eyes,

latin: tam procul esse magis res quaeque remota videtur.
en: the farther off each thing is seen to stand removed.

latin: scilicet haec summe celeri ratione geruntur,
en: Of course these things come about on a principle supremely swift,

latin: quale sit ut videamus, et una quam procul absit.
en: so that we see what a thing is, and at once how far off it stands.

latin: Illud in his rebus minime mirabile habendumst,
en: In these matters it must not be thought at all a wonder

latin: cur, ea quae feriant oculos simulacra videri
en: why, though the images that strike the eyes cannot

latin: singula cum nequeant, res ipsae perspiciantur.
en: be seen one by one, the things themselves are perceived.

latin: ventus enim quoque paulatim cum verberat et cum
en: For when the wind too lashes us little by little, and when

latin: acre fluit frigus, non privam quamque solemus
en: sharp cold flows, we are not used to feel each single

latin: particulam venti sentire et frigoris eius,
en: small part of the wind and of its cold,

latin: sed magis unorsum, fierique perinde videmus
en: but rather the whole at once, and we see blows come about

latin: corpore tum plagas in nostro tam quam aliquae res
en: then on our body just as if some thing were

latin: verberet atque sui det sensum corporis extra.
en: lashing it and giving a sense of its own body outside.

latin: praeterea lapidem digito cum tundimus, ipsum
en: Again, when we strike a stone with a finger, we touch

latin: tangimus extremum saxi summumque colorem
en: the very outermost surface of the rock, its uppermost color,

latin: nec sentimus eum tactu, verum magis ipsam
en: yet we do not feel that by touch; rather we feel

latin: duritiem penitus saxi sentimus in alto.
en: the hardness itself, deep within the rock, far down.

latin: Nunc age, cur ultra speculum videatur imago
en: Come now, learn why the image is seen beyond the mirror;

latin: percipe: nam certe penitus remmota videtur.
en: for certainly it is seen withdrawn deep within.

latin: quod genus illa foris quae vere transpiciuntur,
en: It is like those things outside that are truly seen through

latin: ianua cum per se transpectum praebet apertum,
en: when a doorway offers through itself an open view

latin: multa facitque foris ex aedibus ut videantur;
en: and lets many things outside be seen from within the house;

latin: is quoque enim duplici geminoque fit aereaëre visus.
en: for that sight too comes about through a double, twin air.

latin: primus enim citra postes tum cernitur aeraër,
en: For first, on this side of the doorposts, the air is discerned,

latin: inde fores ipsae dextra laevaque secuntur,
en: next the doors themselves follow, to right and left,

latin: post extraria lux oculos perterget et aeraër
en: after that an outer light sweeps through the eyes, and a second

latin: alter, et illa foris quae vere transpiciuntur.
en: air, and those things outside that are truly seen through.

latin: sic ubi se primum speculi proiecit imago,
en: So, when the image of the mirror first has cast itself forth,

latin: dum venit ad nostras acies, protrudit agitque
en: while it comes to our sight, it thrusts and drives along

latin: aeraaëra qui inter se cumquest oculosque locatus,
en: all the air that is set between itself and our eyes,

latin: et facit, ut prius hunc omnem sentire queamus
en: and brings it about that we can perceive all this air

latin: quam speculum; sed ubi in speculum quoque sensimus ipsum,
en: before the mirror; but when we have perceived the mirror too,

latin: continuo a nobis in eum quae fertur imago
en: at once the image that is carried from us into it

latin: pervenit, et nostros oculos reiecta revisit
en: arrives, and, thrown back, revisits our eyes,

latin: atque alium prae se propellens aeraaëra volvit,
en: and, driving another air before it, rolls it on,

latin: et facit ut prius hunc quam se videamus, eoque
en: and makes us see this air before itself, and for that reason

latin: distare ab speculo tantum semota videtur.
en: it seems to stand removed from the mirror by just so much.

latin: quare etiam atque etiam minime mirarier est par
en: Therefore again and again it is right to wonder not at all

latin: illis quae reddunt speculorum ex aequore visum,
en: at those that give back a sight from the level surface of mirrors,

latin: aeribusaëribus binis quoniam res confit utraque.
en: since in either case the thing is brought about by two airs.

latin: Nunc ea quae nobis membrorum dextera pars est,
en: Now, that part of our limbs which is on the right

latin: in speculis fit ut in laeva videatur eo quod
en: comes to be seen in mirrors on the left, because

latin: planitiem ad speculi veniens cum offendit imago,
en: when the image, coming, strikes against the mirror's flat,

latin: non convertitur incolumis, sed recta retrorsum
en: it is not turned about unharmed, but is dashed straight

latin: sic eliditur, ut siquis, prius arida quam sit
en: backward, as if someone, before it was dry,

latin: cretea persona, adlidat pilaeve trabive,
en: should dash a clay mask against a pillar or a beam,

latin: atque ea continuo rectam si fronte figuram
en: and it should at once keep its features straight in front

latin: servet et elisam retro sese exprimat ipsa.
en: and, dashed back, should press out its own form in reverse.

latin: fiet ut, ante oculus fuerit qui dexter, ut idem
en: It will come about that the eye that was the right before

latin: nunc sit laevus et e laevo sit mutua dexter.
en: is now the left, and the left in exchange the right.

latin: Fit quoque de speculo in speculum ut tradatur imago,
en: It comes about too that an image is passed from mirror to mirror,

latin: quinque etiam aut sex ut fieri simulacra suerintsuërint.
en: so that even five or six images are accustomed to be made.

latin: nam quae cumque retro parte interiore latebunt,
en: For whatever things lie hidden back in the inner part of a house,

latin: inde tamen, quamvis torte penitusque remota,
en: even so, however crookedly and deep withdrawn they lie,

latin: omnia per flexos aditus educta licebit
en: all can be brought out through crooked passages

latin: pluribus haec speculis videantur in aedibus esse.
en: and by many mirrors be seen to be within the house.

latin: usque adeo speculo in speculum translucet imago,
en: So thoroughly does the image shine across from mirror to mirror,

latin: et cum laeva data est, fit rusum ut dextera fiat,
en: and when it is handed on as left, it becomes right again,

latin: inde retro rursum redit et convertit eodem.
en: then it turns back again and returns to the same.

latin: Quin etiam quae cumque latuscula sunt speculorum
en: Further, whatever little sides of mirrors there are

latin: adsimili lateris flexura praedita nostri,
en: endowed with a curvature like that of our own side

latin: dextera ea propter nobis simulacra remittunt,
en: send back to us images that are right on that account,

latin: aut quia de speculo in speculum transfertur imago,
en: either because the image is carried across from mirror to mirror

latin: inde ad nos elisa bis advolat, aut etiam quod
en: and from there, dashed twice, flies to us, or else because

latin: circum agitur, cum venit, imago propterea quod
en: the image is whirled around as it comes, since

latin: flexa figura docet speculi convertier ad nos.
en: the curved shape of the mirror teaches it to turn toward us.

latin: Indugredi porro pariter simulacra pedemque
en: Further, that images walk forward in step with us, and set

latin: ponere nobiscum credas gestumque imitari
en: their foot down with ours, you would believe, and imitate our gesture,

latin: propterea quia, de speculi qua parte recedas,
en: because, from whatever part of the mirror you withdraw,

latin: continuo nequeunt illinc simulacra reverti;
en: from there at once the images cannot return;

latin: omnia quandoquidem cogit natura referri
en: since nature compels all things to be carried back

latin: ac resilire ab rebus ad aequos reddita flexus.
en: and to leap back from things, returned at equal angles.

latin: Splendida porro oculi fugitant vitantque tueri.
en: Further, the eyes shun bright things and avoid looking at them.

latin: sol etiam caecat, contra si tendere pergas,
en: The sun even blinds them, if you persist in straining toward it,

latin: propterea quia vis magnast ipsius et alte
en: because its own force is great, and from on high

latin: aeraaëra per purum simulacra feruntur
en: images are carried through the clear air

latin: et feriunt oculos turbantia composituras.
en: and strike the eyes, throwing their structure into confusion.

latin: Praeterea splendor qui cumque est acer adurit
en: Further, whatever brightness is keen often scorches

latin: saepe oculos ideo quod semina possidet ignis
en: the eyes, because it holds many seeds of fire

latin: multa, dolorem oculis quae gignunt insinuando.
en: which, working their way in, beget pain in the eyes.

latin: lurida praeterea fiunt quae cumque tuentur
en: Further, all things turn sallow that are looked upon

latin: arquati, quia luroris de corpore eorum
en: by the jaundiced, since seeds of sallowness from their body

latin: semina multa fluunt simulacris obvia rerum,
en: flow forth in numbers to meet the images of things,

latin: multaque sunt oculis in eorum denique mixta,
en: and many, finally, are mingled in their eyes,

latin: quae contage sua palloribus omnia pingunt.
en: which with their contagion paint all things with pallor.

latin: E tenebris autem quae sunt in luce tuemur
en: Again, from darkness we see the things that are in light

latin: propterea quia, cum propior caliginis aeraër
en: because, when the nearer air of the gloom,

latin: ater init oculos prior et possedit apertos,
en: the black air, enters the eyes first and takes hold of them open,

latin: insequitur candens confestim lucidus aeraër,
en: at once the shining, bright air follows after,

latin: qui quasi purgat eos ac nigras discutit umbras
en: which as it were purges them and scatters the black shadows

latin: aerisaëris illius; nam multis partibus hic est
en: of that air; for this one is by many degrees

latin: mobilior multisque minutior et mage pollens.
en: more mobile, by many finer, and more powerful.

latin: qui simul atque vias oculorum luce replevit
en: As soon as it has filled the eyes' passages with light

latin: atque pate fecit, quas ante obsederat aeraër
en: and opened those that before the air had laid siege to,

latin: ATER, continuo rerum simulacra secuntur,
en: the black air, at once there follow the images of things

latin: quae sita sunt in luce, lacessuntque ut videamus.
en: that are placed in light, and provoke us to see.

latin: quod contra facere in tenebris e luce nequimus
en: This, contrarily, we cannot do from light into darkness,

latin: propterea quia posterior caliginis aeraër
en: because the air of gloom, coming after,

latin: crassior insequitur, qui cuncta foramina complet
en: follows thicker, and fills up all the openings

latin: obsiditque vias oculorum, ne simulacra
en: and besieges the eyes' passages, so that the images

latin: possint ullarum rerum coniecta moveri.
en: of any things, cast in, cannot be stirred to motion.

latin: Quadratasque procul turris cum cernimus urbis,
en: And when from far off we discern the square towers of a city,

latin: propterea fit uti videantur saepe rutundae,
en: it comes about that they often seem round

latin: angulus optusus quia longe cernitur omnis
en: for this reason: every angle is seen blunted at a distance,

latin: sive etiam potius non cernitur ac perit eius
en: or rather is not seen at all, and its blow

latin: plaga nec ad nostras acies perlabitur ictus,
en: is lost, and its stroke does not glide through to our sight,

latin: aeraaëra per multum quia dum simulacra feruntur,
en: because while the images are carried through much air,

latin: cogit hebescere eum crebris offensibus aeraër.
en: the air by frequent collisions forces the stroke to grow dull.

latin: hoc ubi suffugit sensum simul angulus omnis.
en: When in this way every angle at once has escaped the sense,

latin: fit quasi ut ad turnum saxorum structa tuantur;
en: it comes about that the stone structures look as if turned on a lathe;

latin: non tamen ut coram quae sunt vereque rutunda,
en: not, though, like things that are near at hand and truly round,

latin: sed quasi adumbratim paulum simulata videntur.
en: but they seem a little like them, as if in shadowy sketch.

latin: Umbra videtur item nobis in sole moveri
en: A shadow too seems to us to move in the sun

latin: et vestigia nostra sequi gestumque imitari,
en: and to follow our footsteps and imitate our gesture,

latin: aeraaëra si credis privatum lumine posse
en: if you believe that air deprived of light can

latin: indugredi, motus hominum gestumque sequentem;
en: walk forward, following the motions and gesture of men;

latin: nam nihil esse potest aliud nisi lumine cassus
en: for it can be nothing else but air bereft of light,

latin: aeraër id quod nos umbram perhibere suemussuëmus.
en: this thing that we are accustomed to call shadow.

latin: ni mirum, quia terra locis ex ordine certis
en: Doubtless, because the earth, in places in fixed order,

latin: lumine privatur solis qua cumque meantes
en: is deprived of the sun's light wherever we, moving,

latin: officimus, repletur item quod liquimus eius,
en: get in its way, and is filled again where we have left it,

latin: propterea fit uti videatur, quae fuit umbra
en: it comes about that what was the shadow of the body

latin: corporis, e regione eadem nos usque secuta.
en: seems, the same one, to have followed us straight on all along.

latin: semper enim nova se radiorum lumina fundunt
en: For always new light of rays pours itself forth,

latin: primaque dispereunt, quasi in ignem lana trahatur.
en: and the first perishes, as if wool were drawn into fire.

latin: propterea facile et spoliatur lumine terra
en: Therefore the earth is easily both stripped of light

latin: et repletur item nigrasque sibi abluit umbras.
en: and filled again, and washes its black shadows from itself.

latin: Nec tamen hic oculos falli concedimus hilum.
en: Yet we do not grant that the eyes are deceived one whit in this.

latin: nam quo cumque loco sit lux atque umbra tueri
en: For to see in what place there is light and shadow

latin: illorum est; eadem vero sint lumina necne,
en: is their task; but whether the lights are the same or not,

latin: umbraque quae fuit hic eadem nunc transeat illuc,
en: and whether the shadow that was here now passes over there,

latin: an potius fiat paulo quod diximus ante,
en: or rather what we described a little before comes about,

latin: hoc animi demum ratio discernere debet,
en: this the reasoning of the mind alone must discern,

latin: nec possunt oculi naturam noscere rerum.
en: nor can the eyes come to know the nature of things.

latin: proinde animi vitium hoc oculis adfingere noli.
en: Do not, then, fasten this fault of the mind upon the eyes.

latin: Qua vehimur navi, fertur, cum stare videtur;
en: The ship in which we are carried moves while it seems to stand still;

latin: quae manet in statione, ea praeter creditur ire.
en: the one that stays at its mooring is believed to be going past.

latin: et fugere ad puppim colles campique videntur,
en: And hills and plains seem to flee astern

latin: quos agimus praeter navem velisque volamus.
en: as we drive past them in our ship and fly under sail.

latin: Sidera cessare aetheriis adfixa cavernis
en: The stars all seem to rest, fixed fast to the vaults of the ether,

latin: cuncta videntur, et adsiduo sunt omnia motu,
en: and yet all of them are in unceasing motion,

latin: quandoquidem longos obitus exorta revisunt,
en: since, once risen, they go back to their far-off settings

latin: cum permensa suo sunt caelum corpore claro.
en: when they have measured out the sky with their bright bodies.

latin: solque pari ratione manere et luna videtur
en: And on a like principle the sun and the moon seem to stay

latin: in statione, ea quae ferri res indicat ipsa.
en: at rest, though the fact itself shows that they are carried on.

latin: Exstantisque procul medio de gurgite montis
en: And mountains that stand out far off from the middle of the sea,

latin: classibus inter quos liber patet exitus ingens,
en: between which a wide passage lies open, free for fleets,

latin: insula coniunctis tamen ex his una videtur.
en: seem nonetheless to make one island, joined together.

latin: atria versari et circum cursare columnae
en: That the halls turn round and the columns run in circles

latin: usque adeo fit uti pueris videantur, ubi ipsi
en: seems so strongly to children, once they themselves

latin: desierunt verti, vix ut iam credere possint
en: have stopped spinning, that they can hardly now believe

latin: non supra sese ruere omnia tecta minari.
en: the whole roof is not threatening to fall in on them.

latin: Iamque rubrum tremulis iubar ignibus erigere alte
en: Again, when nature begins to raise on high the red radiance

latin: cum coeptat natura supraque extollere montes,
en: with its trembling fires, and to lift it above the mountains,

latin: quos tibi tum supra sol montis esse videtur
en: those mountains above which the sun then seems to you to be,

latin: comminus ipse suo contingens fervidus igni,
en: touching them close at hand, burning, with its own fire,

latin: vix absunt nobis missus bis mille sagittae,
en: are scarcely two thousand bowshots away from us,

latin: vix etiam cursus quingentos saepe veruti;
en: often scarcely even five hundred casts of a javelin;

latin: inter eos solemque iacent immania ponti
en: between them and the sun lie the immense levels

latin: aequora substrata aetheriis ingentibus oris,
en: of the sea, spread out beneath the vast shores of the ether,

latin: interiectaque sunt terrarum milia multa,
en: and many thousands of lands lie in between,

latin: quae variae retinent gentes et saecla ferarum.
en: held by various peoples and the generations of wild beasts.

latin: At coniectus aquae digitum non altior unum,
en: But a pool of water no deeper than a single finger,

latin: qui lapides inter sistit per strata viarum,
en: which stands between the stones of the paving in the streets,

latin: despectum praebet sub terras inpete tanto,
en: offers a view down beneath the earth to a depth as great

latin: a terris quantum caeli patet altus hiatus,
en: as the high gulf of the sky gapes open above the earth,

latin: nubila despicere et caelum ut videare videre,
en: so that you seem to look down on clouds and to see the sky,

latin: corpora mirande sub terras abdita caelo.
en: and bodies wonderfully hidden in a sky beneath the earth.

latin: Denique ubi in medio nobis ecus acer obhaesit
en: Again, when our spirited horse has stuck fast in midstream

latin: flumine et in rapidas amnis despeximus undas,
en: and we have looked down into the river's rushing waves,

latin: stantis equi corpus transversum ferre videtur
en: some force seems to carry the body of the standing horse

latin: vis et in adversum flumen contrudere raptim,
en: sideways and to thrust it swiftly against the current,

latin: et quo cumque oculos traiecimus omnia ferri
en: and wherever we cast our eyes, all things seem

latin: et fluere adsimili nobis ratione videntur.
en: to be carried and to flow on, to us, in the same way.

latin: Porticus aequali quamvis est denique ductu
en: Again, though a colonnade runs in an even line

latin: stansque in perpetuum paribus suffulta columnis,
en: and stands from end to end propped on equal columns,

latin: longa tamen parte ab summa cum tota videtur,
en: yet when it is seen, all its length, from the top end,

latin: paulatim trahit angusti fastigia coni,
en: it gradually draws into the point of a narrow cone,

latin: tecta solo iungens atque omnia dextera laevis
en: joining roof to floor and all the right side to the left,

latin: donec in obscurum coni conduxit acumen.
en: until it has drawn them into the dim tip of the cone.

latin: In pelago nautis ex undis ortus in undis
en: On the open sea, to sailors the sun, risen from the waves,

latin: sol fit uti videatur obire et condere lumen;
en: seems to set in the waves and to hide its light;

latin: quippe ubi nil aliud nisi aquam caelumque tuentur;
en: for indeed they see nothing else but water and sky;

latin: ne leviter credas labefactari undique sensus.
en: lest you lightly believe the senses are shaken on every side.

latin: at maris ignaris in portu clauda videntur
en: But to those who do not know the sea, ships in harbor

latin: navigia aplustris fractis obnitier undis.
en: seem crippled, their stern-posts broken, as they strain against the waves.

latin: nam quae cumque supra rorem salis edita pars est
en: For whatever part of the oars is raised above the brine

latin: remorum, recta est, et recta superne guberna;
en: is straight, and the rudders are straight above;

latin: quae demersa liquore obeunt, refracta videntur
en: but the parts that go down sunk in the water seem broken back,

latin: omnia converti sursumque supina reverti
en: all turned about and bent, returning upward, upside down,

latin: et reflexa prope in summo fluitare liquore.
en: and so bent back as almost to float on the water's surface.

latin: Raraque per caelum cum venti nubila portant
en: And when the winds carry thin clouds across the sky

latin: tempore nocturno, tum splendida signa videntur
en: in the night-time, then the shining constellations seem

latin: labier adversum nimbos atque ire superne
en: to glide against the clouds and to travel above them

latin: longe aliam in partem ac vera ratione feruntur
en: in a far other direction than true reasoning shows they are carried.

latin: At si forte oculo manus uni subdita supter
en: But if by chance a hand placed beneath one eye

latin: pressit eum, quodam sensu fit uti videantur
en: presses it from below, by a certain feeling it comes about

latin: omnia quae tuimur fieri tum bina tuendo,
en: that all things we look at seem, as we look, to become double:

latin: bina lucernarum florentia lumina flammis
en: double the lights of the lamps, flowering with flames,

latin: binaque per totas aedis geminare supellex
en: and through the whole house the furniture doubled in pairs,

latin: et duplicis hominum facies et corpora bina.
en: and men with double faces and twin bodies.

latin: Denique cum suavi devinxit membra sopore
en: Again, when sleep has bound our limbs in sweet slumber

latin: somnus et in summa corpus iacet omne quiete,
en: and the whole body lies in deepest rest,

latin: tum vigilare tamen nobis et membra movere
en: yet we seem to ourselves to be awake and to move

latin: nostra videmur, et in noctis caligine caeca
en: our limbs, and in the blind darkness of the night

latin: cernere censemus solem lumenque diurnum,
en: we think we see the sun and the light of day,

latin: conclusoque loco caelum mare flumina montis
en: and, in a closed room, sky, sea, rivers, mountains

latin: mutare et campos pedibus transire videmur,
en: we seem to change, and to cross the plains on foot,

latin: et sonitus audire, severa silentia noctis
en: and to hear sounds, when the stern silences of the night

latin: undique cum constent, et reddere dicta tacentes.
en: hold fast on every side, and to give answers, saying nothing.

latin: Cetera de genere hoc mirande multa videmus,
en: We see many other wonders of this kind,

latin: quae violare fidem quasi sensibus omnia quaerunt,

latin: ne quiquam, quoniam pars horum maxima fallit
en: in vain, since the greatest part of them deceive

latin: propter opinatus animi, quos addimus ipsi,

latin: pro visis ut sint quae non sunt sensibus visa;
en: so that things not seen by the senses pass for seen;

latin: nam nihil aegrius est quam res secernere apertas
en: for nothing is harder than to separate things plain

latin: ab dubiis, animus quas ab se protinus addit.

latin: Denique nil sciri siquis putat, id quoque nescit
en: Again, if anyone thinks that nothing can be known, he does not know

latin: an sciri possit, quoniam nil scire fatetur.

latin: hunc igitur contra minuam contendere causam,
en: Against this man, then, I will forbear to argue the case,

latin: qui capite ipse suo in statuit vestigia sese.

latin: et tamen hoc quoque uti concedam scire, at id ipsum
en: And yet, granting that he knows even this, still I would ask

latin: quaeram, cum in rebus veri nil viderit ante,

latin: unde sciat quid sit scire et nescire vicissim,

latin: notitiam veri quae res falsique crearit
en: what thing has created the notion of the true and the false,

latin: et dubium certo quae res differre probarit.

latin: invenies primis ab sensibus esse creatam
en: You will find that from the senses first was created

latin: notitiem veri neque sensus posse refelli.
en: the notion of the true, and that the senses cannot be refuted.

latin: nam maiore fide debet reperirier illud,
en: For that must be found to deserve greater trust

latin: sponte sua veris quod possit vincere falsa.

latin: quid maiore fide porro quam sensus haberi
en: Further, what ought to be held in greater trust than the senses?

latin: debet? an ab sensu falso ratio orta valebit

latin: dicere eos contra, quae tota ab sensibus orta est?

latin: qui nisi sunt veri, ratio quoque falsa fit omnis.

latin: An poterunt oculos aures reprehendere, an aures
en: Or will the ears be able to correct the eyes, or touch

latin: tactus? an hunc porro tactum sapor arguet oris,
en: the ears? Or again will the mouth's taste accuse this touch,

latin: an confutabunt nares oculive revincent?
en: or will the nostrils confute it, or the eyes refute it?

latin: non, ut opinor, ita est. nam seorsum cuique potestas
en: It is not so, I think. For to each a separate power

latin: divisast, sua vis cuiquest, ideoque necesse est
en: has been allotted, each has its own force, and so it must be

latin: et quod molle sit et gelidum fervensve videre
en: that what is soft, and cold or hot, is perceived apart,

latin: et seorsum varios rerum sentire colores
en: and that the various colors of things are perceived apart,

latin: et quae cumque coloribus sint coniuncta necessest.
en: and whatever things are joined to colors.

latin: seorsus item sapor oris habet vim, seorsus odores
en: Apart, likewise, the mouth's taste has its power, apart smells

latin: nascuntur, seorsum sonitus. ideoque necesse est
en: are born, apart sounds. And so it must be

latin: non possint alios alii convincere sensus.
en: that one sense cannot convict another.

latin: nec porro poterunt ipsi reprehendere sese,
en: Nor, further, will they be able to correct themselves,

latin: aequa fides quoniam debebit semper haberi.
en: since equal trust must always be placed in them.

latin: proinde quod in quoquest his visum tempore, verumst.
en: Therefore what has seemed to them at any time is true.

latin: Et si non poterit ratio dissolvere causam,
en: And if reasoning cannot untie the cause

latin: cur ea quae fuerint iuxtim quadrata, procul sint
en: why things that were square close at hand are seen far off

latin: visa rutunda, tamen praestat rationis egentem
en: as round, still it is better, if you are at a loss for reasoning,

latin: reddere mendose causas utriusque figurae,
en: to give faulty causes for each of the two shapes

latin: quam manibus manifesta suis emittere quoquam
en: than to let things plain to see slip from your hands somewhere

latin: et violare fidem primam et convellere tota
en: and violate the first trust and tear up all

latin: fundamenta quibus nixatur vita salusque.

latin: non modo enim ratio ruat omnis, vita quoque ipsa
en: For not only would all reasoning fall in ruin; life itself

latin: concidat extemplo, nisi credere sensibus ausis

latin: praecipitisque locos vitare et cetera quae sint
en: and avoid steep places and the other things that are

latin: in genere hoc fugienda, sequi contraria quae sint.
en: to be fled in this kind, and follow what is their opposite.

latin: illa tibi est igitur verborum copia cassa
en: That whole store of words, then, is empty for you,

latin: omnis, quae contra sensus instructa paratast.
en: which is drawn up and made ready against the senses.

latin: Denique ut in fabrica, si pravast regula prima,
en: Finally, as in a building, if the first rule is crooked,

latin: normaque si fallax rectis regionibus exit,
en: and if the square is false and slips from its straight lines,

latin: et libella aliqua si ex parti claudicat hilum,
en: and if the level limps a hair's breadth at any point,

latin: omnia mendose fieri atque obstipa necessu est
en: everything must be made faulty and askew,

latin: prava cubantia prona supina atque absona tecta,
en: the house crooked, sagging, leaning forward, leaning back, out of true,

latin: iam ruere ut quaedam videantur velle, ruantque
en: so that some parts seem already to want to fall, and do fall,

latin: prodita iudiciis fallacibus omnia primis,
en: all of it betrayed by those first false judgments;

latin: sic igitur ratio tibi rerum prava necessest
en: so then your reasoning of things must be crooked

latin: falsaque sit, falsis quae cumque ab sensibus ortast.
en: and false, whatever reasoning has risen from false senses.

latin: Nunc alii sensus quo pacto quisque suam rem
en: Now, by what means each of the other senses perceives

latin: sentiat, haud quaquam ratio scruposa relicta est.
en: its own object, the reasoning left is by no means rugged.

latin: Principio auditur sonus et vox omnis, in auris
en: First of all, sound and every voice are heard when, working their way

latin: insinuata suo pepulere ubi corpore sensum.
en: into the ears, they have struck the sense with their body.

latin: corpoream quoque enim vocem constare fatendumst
en: For we must admit that voice too, and sound, are bodily,

latin: et sonitum, quoniam possunt inpellere sensus.
en: since they are able to strike upon the senses.

latin: Praeterea radit vox fauces saepe facitque
en: Further, the voice often scrapes the throat, and shouting

latin: asperiora foras gradiens arteria clamor,
en: makes the windpipe rougher as it goes out,

latin: quippe per angustum turba maiore coorta
en: since, whenever in a greater crowd through a narrow way

latin: ire foras ubi coeperunt primordia vocum.
en: the first-beginnings of voices, risen, have begun to go out.

latin: scilicet expletis quoque ianua raditur oris.
en: Clearly the door of the mouth too is scraped when it is filled.

latin: haud igitur dubiumst quin voces verbaque constent
en: There is no doubt, then, that voices and words consist

latin: corporeis e principiis, ut laedere possint.
en: of bodily beginnings, since they are able to do harm.

latin: nec te fallit item quid corporis auferat et quid
en: Nor, likewise, does it escape you what body is lost, and what

latin: detrahat ex hominum nervis ac viribus ipsis
en: is drawn from men's sinews and their very strength

latin: perpetuus sermo nigrai noctis ad umbram
en: by unbroken speech carried on to the shadow of black night

latin: aurorae perductus ab exoriente nitore,
en: from the rising brightness of the dawn,

latin: praesertim si cum summost clamore profusus.
en: above all if it is poured out with the loudest shouting.

latin: ergo corpoream vocem constare necessest,
en: Therefore the voice must be bodily,

latin: multa loquens quoniam amittit de corpore partem.
en: since one who talks much loses part of his body.

latin: Asperitas autem vocis fit ab asperitate
en: Roughness of voice, again, comes from roughness

latin: principiorum et item levor levore creatur;
en: of the beginnings, and smoothness likewise is made by smoothness;

latin: nec simili penetrant auris primordia forma,
en: nor do the first-beginnings pierce the ears with like shape

latin: cum tuba depresso graviter sub murmure mugit
en: when the trumpet bellows deep with its low-pressed growl

latin: et reboat raucum retro cita barbita bombum,
en: and the barbarous horn, roused, booms back its hoarse drone,

latin: et iam Dauliades natae hortis ex Heliconis
en: and when the Daulian birds, born in the gardens of Helicon,

latin: cum liquidam tollunt lugubri voce querellam.
en: raise their liquid lament with mourning voice.

latin: Hasce igitur penitus voces cum corpore nostro
en: So when we press these voices out from deep within our body

latin: exprimimus rectoque foras emittimus ore,
en: and send them out straight through the mouth,

latin: mobilis articulat nervorum daedala lingua,
en: the nimble tongue, artificer of sinews, articulates them,

latin: formaturaque labrorum pro parte figurat.
en: and the shaping of the lips gives them form in its turn.

latin: hoc ubi non longum spatiumst unde illa profecta
en: When the space is not long from which each voice

latin: perveniat vox quaeque, necessest verba quoque ipsa
en: sets out to arrive, the words themselves too must

latin: plane exaudiri discernique articulatim;
en: be heard plainly and distinguished syllable by syllable;

latin: servat enim formaturam servatque figuram.
en: for the voice keeps its shaping and keeps its form.

latin: at si inter positum spatium sit longius aequo,
en: But if the space set between is longer than is fit,

latin: aeraaëra per multum confundi verba necessest
en: the words must be confused passing through much air

latin: et conturbari vocem, dum transvolat auras.
en: and the voice thrown into disorder as it flies through the air.

latin: ergo fit, sonitum ut possis sentire neque illam
en: So it comes about that you can perceive a sound but cannot

latin: internoscere, verborum sententia quae sit;
en: make out what the meaning of the words is;

latin: usque adeo confusa venit vox inque pedita.
en: so confused and tangled does the voice arrive.

latin: Praeterea verbum saepe unum perciet auris
en: Further, a single word often rouses the ears

latin: omnibus in populo missum praeconis ab ore.
en: of all in a crowd, sent out from a crier's mouth.

latin: in multas igitur voces vox una repente
en: One voice, then, suddenly scatters into many voices,

latin: diffugit, in privas quoniam se dividit auris
en: since it divides itself among separate ears,

latin: obsignans formam verbis clarumque sonorem.
en: stamping on the words their form and clear sound.

latin: at quae pars vocum non auris incidit ipsas,
en: But the part of the voices that does not fall on the ears themselves

latin: praeter lata perit frustra diffusa per auras.

latin: pars solidis adlisa locis reiecta sonorem

latin: reddit et inter dum frustratur imagine verbi.

latin: Quae bene cum videas, rationem reddere possis
en: When you see this well, you can give an account

latin: tute tibi atque aliis, quo pacto per loca sola

latin: saxa paris formas verborum ex ordine reddant.
en: rocks give back the matching forms of words in order,

latin: palantis comites com montis inter opacos
en: when we search among the shadowed mountains for straying comrades

latin: quaerimus et magna dispersos voce ciemus.
en: and call them, scattered, with a great voice.

latin: sex etiam aut septem loca vidi reddere vocis,

latin: unam cum iaceres: ita colles collibus ipsi

latin: verba repulsantes iterabant dicta referri.

latin: finitimi fingunt et Faunos esse locuntur,

latin: quorum noctivago strepitu ludoque iocanti
en: by whose night-wandering din and jesting play

latin: adfirmant volgo taciturna silentia rumpi
en: they declare the speechless silences are commonly broken,

latin: chordarumque sonos fieri dulcisque querellas,
en: and sounds of strings arise, and the sweet laments

latin: tibia quas fundit digitis pulsata canentum,
en: that the pipe pours out when struck by the players' fingers;

latin: et genus agricolum late sentiscere, quom Pan

latin: pinea semiferi capitis velamina quassans
en: shaking the pine coverings of his half-beast head,

latin: unco saepe labro calamos percurrit hiantis,

latin: fistula silvestrem ne cesset fundere musam.
en: so that the pipe will not cease pouring out its woodland music.

latin: cetera de genere hoc monstra ac portenta loquontur,
en: Other marvels and portents of this kind they tell,

latin: ne loca deserta ab divis quoque forte putentur

latin: sola tenere. ideo iactant miracula dictis

latin: aut aliqua ratione alia ducuntur, ut omne
en: or they are led by some other reason, as the whole

latin: humanum genus est avidum nimis auricularum.

latin: Quod super est, non est mirandum qua ratione,
en: For the rest, it is no wonder by what principle,

latin: per loca quae nequeunt oculi res cernere apertas,

latin: haec loca per voces veniant aurisque lacessant,

latin: conloquium clausis foribus quoque saepe videmus;

latin: ni mirum quia vox per flexa foramina rerum

latin: incolumis transire potest, simulacra renutant;

latin: perscinduntur enim, nisi recta foramina tranant,

en: such as those of glass, through which every appearance flies.

latin: praeterea partis in cunctas dividitur vox,

latin: ex aliis aliae quoniam gignuntur, ubi una

latin: dissuluit semel in multas exorta, quasi ignis

latin: saepe solet scintilla suos se spargere in ignis.
en: often spreads itself out into its own fires.

latin: ergo replentur loca vocibus abdita retro,
en: Therefore places hidden away behind are filled with voices,

latin: omnia quae circum fervunt sonituque cientur.
en: and all the places round about are astir and roused with sound.

latin: at simulacra viis derectis omnia tendunt,
en: But images all travel along straight paths

latin: ut sunt missa semel; qua propter cernere nemo
en: once they are sent out; and so no one can see

latin: saepe supra potis est, at voces accipere extra.

latin: et tamen ipsa quoque haec, dum transit clausa domorum
en: And yet this very voice too, while it passes through the closed rooms

latin: vox optunditur atque auris confusa penetrat
en: of houses, is blunted and enters the ears confused,

latin: et sonitum potius quam verba audire videmur.
en: and we seem to hear a sound rather than words.

latin: Hoc, qui sentimus sucum, lingua atque palatum
en: As for how we perceive flavor, the tongue and palate

latin: plusculum habent in se rationis, plus operai.
en: hold a little more reasoning in them, and more labor.

latin: principio sucum sentimus in ore, cibum cum
en: To begin with, we perceive flavor in the mouth when, chewing,

latin: mandendo exprimimus, ceu plenam spongiam aquai

latin: siquis forte manu premere ac siccare coepitcoëpit.

latin: inde quod exprimimus per caulas omne palati

latin: diditur et rarae per flexa foramina linguae,

latin: hoc ubi levia sunt manantis corpora suci,

latin: suaviter attingunt et suaviter omnia tractant

latin: umida linguai circum sudantia templa;

latin: deinde voluptas est e suco fine palati;

latin: nec refert quicquam quo victu corpus alatur,

latin: dum modo quod capias concoctum didere possis

latin: Nunc aliis alius qui sit cibus ut videamus,

latin: hoc tamen esse aliis possit perdulce videri,

latin: tantaque in his rebus distantia differitasque est,

latin: ut quod aliis cibus est aliis fuat acre venenum;
en: that what is food to some is to others sharp poison;

latin: est itaque ut serpens, hominis quae tacta salivis
en: and so there is a snake which, touched by a man's spittle,

latin: disperit ac sese mandendo conficit ipsa.
en: perishes and destroys itself by gnawing at itself.

latin: praeterea nobis veratrum est acre venenum,
en: Further, hellebore is sharp poison to us,

latin: at capris adipes et cocturnicibus auget.
en: but to goats and to quails it adds fat.

latin: id quibus ut fiat rebus cognoscere possis,
en: So that you can learn by what means this comes about,

latin: principio meminisse decet quae diximus ante,
en: first it is fitting to remember what we said before,

latin: semina multimodis in rebus mixta teneri.
en: that seeds are held mixed in things in many ways.

latin: porro omnes quae cumque cibum capiunt animantes,

latin: ut sunt dissimiles extrinsecus et generatim
en: just as they are unlike outwardly, and, kind by kind,

latin: extima membrorum circumcaesura coercetcoërcet,

latin: proinde et seminibus constant variantque figura.

latin: semina cum porro distent, differre necessest
en: Again, since the seeds differ, it must be that the intervals

latin: intervalla viasque, foramina quae perhibemus,

latin: omnibus in membris et in ore ipsoque palato.

latin: esse minora igitur quaedam maioraque debent,
en: Therefore some must be smaller and some larger,

latin: esse triquetra aliis, aliis quadrata necessest,
en: for some creatures they must be three-cornered, for others square,

latin: multa rutunda, modis multis multangula quaedam.
en: many round, some many-angled in many ways.

latin: namque figurarum ratio ut motusque reposcunt,
en: For as the order of the shapes and their motions demand,

latin: proinde foraminibus debent differe figurae
en: so the shapes of the pores must differ,

latin: et variare viae proinde ac textura coercetcoërcet.

latin: hoc ubi quod suave est aliis aliis fit amarum,
en: So when what is sweet to some becomes bitter to others,

latin: illi, cui suave est, levissima corpora debent
en: for the one to whom it is sweet the smoothest bodies must

latin: contractabiliter caulas intrare palati,
en: enter the passages of the palate caressingly,

latin: at contra quibus est eadem res intus acerba,
en: but for those to whom the same thing is bitter within,

latin: aspera ni mirum penetrant hamataque fauces.
en: rough and hooked bodies, doubtless, make their way into the throat.

latin: nunc facile est ex his rebus cognoscere quaeque.

latin: quippe ubi cui febris bili superante coorta est
en: For indeed when fever has risen in someone, the bile prevailing,

latin: aut alia ratione aliquast vis excita morbi,

latin: perturbatur ibi iam totum corpus et omnes
en: then the whole body is thrown into disorder, and all

latin: commutantur ibi positurae principiorum;

latin: fit prius ad sensum ut quae corpora conveniebant

latin: nunc non conveniant, et cetera sint magis apta,
en: now do not suit it, and others are more fitted,

latin: quae penetrata queunt sensum progignere acerbum;

latin: utraque enim sunt in mellis commixta sapore;

latin: id quod iam supera tibi saepe ostendimus ante.

latin: Nunc age, quo pacto naris adiectus odoris
en: Come now, how the touch of odor strikes the nostrils

latin: tangat agam. primum res multas esse necessest
en: I shall set out. First, there must be many things

latin: unde fluens volvat varius se fluctus odorum,
en: from which a varied stream of odors rolls flowing,

latin: et fluere et mitti volgo spargique putandumst;
en: and we must suppose they flow and are sent out and scattered everywhere;

latin: verum aliis alius magis est animantibus aptus,
en: but one odor is more fitted to some creatures, another to others,

latin: dissimilis propter formas. ideoque per auras
en: because of their unlike forms. And so through the air

latin: mellis apes quamvis longe ducuntur odore,
en: bees are drawn, however far, by the odor of honey,

latin: volturiique cadaveribus; tum fissa ferarum
